types.name: git_repository_item_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum GITDIR 0 .. WORKTREE_CONFIG 14 plus the sentinel GIT_REPOSITORY_ITEM__LAST 15 (bindgen: c_uint). No storage, pointers or lifecycle: passed by value only. Sole public consumer git_repository_item_path (repository.c:3311 -> git_repository__item_path, :3319) indexes the static items[15] table (repository.c:46, {parent, fallback, name, directory}) with the value UNCHECKED: __LAST and every larger value read out of bounds (UBSan 'index 15 out of bounds for type ...[15]' at repository.c:3323, confirmed with the asan-ubsan build, batch 9 of libgit2/repository wave 0, 2026-10-10). Within bounds, resolved_parent_path maps the parent GITDIR/WORKDIR/COMMONDIR to git_repository_path/workdir/commondir (any other parent value: GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid item directory', unreachable from the table); a NULL parent falls back to the entry's fallback (GITDIR for the commondir-rooted items and WORKTREE_CONFIG), else GIT_ENOTFOUND + GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'path cannot exist in repository' (WORKDIR of a bare repo). Directories get a trailing '/'; the commondir link is resolved (worktree COMMONDIR = main/.git/). Internal callers pass named constants only. Rust: `Item` (#[repr(u32)], #[non_exhaustive], 15 variants, no sentinel) with `ALL` indexed by value, fallible `from_raw`/TryFrom (UnnamedItem) refusing >= __LAST, in repository/repository.rs.

types.name: git_repository_new_options
types._comment_agent: Pointer-free 8-byte options value (version + git_oid_t), never allocated or freed by libgit2; read-only by git_repository_new_ext (version check, then GIT_ASSERT_ARG(git_oid_type_is_valid) for a non-zero oid_type: an unnamed value aborts the Debug/coverage build and fails -1 otherwise). 0 = GIT_OID_DEFAULT. Wrapped as NewOptions (repository/sys/repository.rs) with an Option<OidType> setter so only 0 or a named type is stored.

types.name: git_repository_open_flag_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless bit-flag enum NO_SEARCH 1, CROSS_FS 2, BARE 4, NO_DOTGIT 8, FROM_ENV 16 (bindgen: c_uint). No storage, pointers or lifecycle. Consumed as the `unsigned int flags` of git_repository_open_ext (repository.c:1157; find_repo/find_repo_traverse/lookup_commondir/is_valid_repository_path take it as uint32_t) and internally by git_repository_open (NO_SEARCH), git_repository_discover (CROSS_FS when across_fs), submodule.c:1635 (NO_SEARCH|BARE) and the CLI (FROM_ENV). Only the five named bits are tested; any other bit is ignored (equivalence-tested with 1<<5|1<<31). Observed semantics that differ from the header: FROM_ENV does NOT ignore the other flags (NO_SEARCH/BARE still apply) and replaces ceiling_dirs only when it is NULL; BARE (like NO_DOTGIT) makes the first iteration try start_path itself without appending .git (so a working dir with BARE|NO_SEARCH is ENOTFOUND), parents still get .git first; BARE also leaves no workdir. Cross-enum quirk: repo_init_config (repository.c:2377) tests GIT_REPOSITORY_OPEN_FROM_ENV (1<<4) against git_repository_init_options.flags, where 1<<4 is GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_MKPATH, so MKPATH makes init's symlink probe (are_symlinks_supported, repository.c:2236) load the system/global config from the GIT_CONFIG_* environment; the parameter is GIT_UNUSED outside GIT_WIN32, so only Windows builds observe it. Rust: `OpenFlag` (#[repr(u32)], #[non_exhaustive], fallible from_raw/TryFrom, UnnamedOpenFlag) and the `OpenFlags(c_uint)` set (from_bits_retain keeps unnamed bits, bits/unnamed_bits/contains/insert/remove/iter, BitOr, FromIterator, Debug) in repository/repository.rs.

types.name: git_repository_state_t
types._comment_agent: Plain C enum, values 0..=11, no lifecycle. Its only producer is git_repository_state, which returns it as an int (or -1 when copying the gitdir path fails); reset.c compares it against MERGE/REVERT/CHERRYPICK. Wrapped as a fieldless RepositoryState, converted fallibly from a raw value; GIT_REPOSITORY_STATE_NONE is the Clean variant.

types.name: git_signature
types._comment_agent: git_signature is a heap object owned by a single holder: CBox<Signature, SignatureFree> (git_signature_free drops it with both strings; git_signature_dup deep-copies it, refusing NULL fields that C would strdup). Public consumers otherwise receive `const git_signature *` borrowed from a parent (git_commit_author/committer, git_tag_tagger, git_note_author/committer, git_reflog_entry_committer, git_blame_hunk fields) and only read it; every `const git_signature *` argument (commit/tag/note/reflog/stash/rebase creation) is only read and copied, so a caller-built struct over borrowed strings (SignatureView) is a valid argument. `when` is an embedded git_time value. No refcount, no lock. Constructors: git_signature_new, git_signature_now, git_signature_from_buffer (alloc through out-param), git_signature_default / git_signature_default_from_env (need a git_repository; left to the object/signature symbol batch). C defects: git_signature_new leaks p (and p->name) when a string allocation fails; git_signature_dup leaks the partial copy on OOM; git_signature_default_from_env frees author/committer with git__free on error, leaking their strings.

ptr.note: NUL-terminated author email; same ownership as `name`: allocated by git_signature_new / from_buffer / dup from libgit2's allocator and freed by git_signature_free with git__free; pool-borrowed only in git_transaction's internal git_signature__pdup copies. NULL after an allocation failure inside git_signature__parse (unchecked extract_trimmed), which git_signature_dup and the commit writer then dereference. Never written through.

NUL-terminated author name. Owned on every public path: git_signature_new / git_signature_from_buffer (git__substrdup via extract_trimmed) and git_signature_dup (git__strdup) allocate it from libgit2's allocator, and git_signature_free releases it with git__free (also called by git_commit__free, git_tag__free, git_reflog_entry__free, git_note_free, free_hunk on the signatures those objects own). Borrowed only in the internal git_signature__pdup copies a git_transaction keeps in its pool (transaction.c copy_common / dup_reflog), which are never freed individually and never reach a public consumer. Nullable: git_signature__parse does not check extract_trimmed's result, so an allocation failure leaves it NULL while the parse (git_signature_from_buffer, commit/tag/reflog parsing) still succeeds; refdb_reftable_log_fill checks for that, git_signature_dup (strdup(NULL)) and git_signature__writebuf (%s) do not. A calloc'd signature is NULL before parse. Never written through; libgit2 only reads, copies or frees it. Rust: Option<&CStr> getter on SignatureRef, replacement setters taking an OdbDataStr (git__malloc storage released by git__free) on SignatureMut.

types.name: git_strarray
types._comment_agent: Wrapped in core/strarray.rs (core wave 0 batch 4) as StrArray + StrArrayVal = CVal<StrArray, StrArrayDispose> for the owned form (strings move as OdbDataStrVec), and StrArrayView<'a> for the borrowed input form, which hands out StrArrayRef only. git_strarray_copy (the deep cloner) is hidden under DEPRECATE_HARD, so copies go through OdbDataStrVec::dup_all. git_strarray_dispose is skipped for a NULL `strings` (empty state; see the first-init allocator race).

ptr.note: A buffer of `count` NUL-terminated `char *` elements. Two statically distinct contracts, decided by API direction. (1) OUTPUT (git_reference_list, git_tag_list(_match), git_remote_list, git_worktree_list, git_remote_get_fetch/push_refspecs via copy_refspecs, git_remote_rename problems, GIT_OPT_GET_EXTENSIONS, store_refs): libgit2 writes `strings`/`count` without disposing what the struct held, from a git_vector (git_vector_detach / .contents, i.e. git__reallocarray storage with spare capacity) whose elements are git__strdup'd; the struct owns the array and every string, and git_strarray_dispose frees strings[0..count) then the array with git__free, then zeroes the struct. git_vector_init(&v, 8) allocates eagerly, so an empty result is often a NON-NULL array with count 0 (refs.c, tag.c, remote.c, repository.c extensions); worktree.c and the error paths leave NULL/0. Producers never store a NULL element. (2) INPUT (`const git_strarray *` args: git_index_add_all/remove_all/update_all, git_remote_fetch/push/upload/download/connect, git_reset_default, git_pathspec_new, git_stash_save_with_opts, and by-value option fields: git_diff_options.pathspec, git_checkout_options.paths, custom_headers, remote_push_options): libgit2 only reads strings[0..count) (pathspec/iterator/headers deref every element, so NULL elements are invalid), copies what it keeps (git_strarray_copy, git__strdup), and never frees or writes the caller's array: borrowed for the call / the options' lifetime. git_remote_connect memcpys the caller's struct into its options and copies it via git_remote_connect_options_dup before use. NULL `strings` means empty only with count 0; git_strarray_dispose with NULL strings and count > 0 derefs NULL. Owned arrays are written (dispose zeroes, producers fill), borrowed ones are const.

types.name: git_submodule_ignore_t
types._comment_agent: Values -1 (UNSPECIFIED), 1 NONE, 2 UNTRACKED, 3 DIRTY, 4 ALL; 0 is unnamed (the old GIT_SUBMODULE_IGNORE_DEFAULT the types.h comment still mentions is gone). Consumers: git_submodule_status / git_submodule__status read UNSPECIFIED as 'the submodule's configured value' and compare the rest for equality (any other value behaves like UNTRACKED). git_diff_options.ignore_submodules: `<= 0` (0 from a zeroed struct, or UNSPECIFIED from GIT_DIFF_OPTIONS_INIT) means 'read diff.ignoreSubmodules' (diff_generate.c:561). git_submodule_set_ignore maps through _sm_ignore_map, so UNSPECIFIED, 0 and anything outside 1..4 fail with GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for ignore'. Producers (git_submodule_ignore, git_submodule_parse_ignore from config strings none/untracked/dirty/all/true/false) only return 1..4, plus UNSPECIFIED from git_submodule_ignore(NULL) via GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL. Wrapped as core::types::SubmoduleIgnore (repr(i32)), converted fallibly with from_raw.

types.name: git_submodule_recurse_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_SUBMODULE_RECURSE_NO = 0, _YES = 1, _ONDEMAND = 2, include/git2/types.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. Producers: submodule_parse_recurse (submodule.c:2034) maps .gitmodules/config fetchRecurseSubmodules through _sm_recurse_map (bool false->NO, true->YES, 'on-demand' case-insensitive->ONDEMAND); an unreadable spelling writes YES to *out then fails git_submodule_lookup with GIT_EINVALID 'invalid value for submodule 'recurse' property: '<v>''; an unset setting leaves the alloc default NO (submodule.c:1962). git_submodule_fetch_recurse_submodules returns sm->fetch_recurse unchanged (only named values; NULL sm -> GIT_ASSERT_ARG, NO in release, abort in the Debug/coverage build). Consumer: git_submodule_set_fetch_recurse_submodules -> write_mapped_var -> git_config_lookup_map_enum: unnamed values fail -1 GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for fetchRecurseSubmodules'; YES writes 'true', ONDEMAND 'on-demand', NO (CONFIGMAP_FALSE, str NULL) DELETES the .gitmodules key and so fails GIT_ENOTFOUND (GIT_ERROR_CONFIG 'could not find key 'submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules' to delete') when the key is absent, although the submodule already reads NO. Rust: SubmoduleRecurse in core/types.rs, converted fallibly (from_raw/TryFrom -> UnnamedSubmoduleRecurse), Default = No (unset). The submodule symbol batch should treat that ENOTFOUND as success or pre-check, and route returned values through from_raw.

types.name: git_submodule_update_t
types._comment_agent: Fieldless C enum (GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_CHECKOUT = 1, _REBASE = 2, _MERGE = 3, _NONE = 4, _DEFAULT = 0, include/git2/types.h; bindgen types it c_uint). No storage, no pointers, no lifecycle: passed and returned by value. DEFAULT (0) is never produced and never accepted: git_submodule_parse_update (submodule.c:2020) maps only via _sm_update_map ('checkout','rebase','merge','none' case-insensitive, bool true->CHECKOUT, false->NONE; an unreadable spelling writes CHECKOUT to *out and fails git_submodule_lookup with GIT_EINVALID 'invalid value for submodule 'update' property: '<v>''), an unset setting keeps the alloc default CHECKOUT (submodule.c:1961), git_submodule_update_strategy maps any value < CHECKOUT to CHECKOUT (NULL sm -> GIT_ASSERT_ARG, NONE in release, abort in Debug), and git_submodule_set_update -> write_mapped_var refuses 0 and every other unnamed value with -1 GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE 'invalid value for update'; named values are written to .gitmodules by name ('checkout','rebase','merge','none'). git_submodule_init writes submodule.<name>.update into .git/config via submodule_update_to_str for every value but CHECKOUT (whose entry it removes); its NULL return is unreachable. The header's GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_RESET does not exist. Rust: SubmoduleUpdate in core/types.rs has no variant for DEFAULT (from_raw(0) = None, UnnamedSubmoduleUpdate), Default = Checkout so from_raw(raw).unwrap_or_default() resolves 0 as C does; typed setters can then never send a value C refuses.

types.name: git_tag
types._comment_agent: git_tag is a git_object of type tag (first member `object`; casts both ways in object_api.c). It is opaque in the public API and refcounted through the embedded git_cached_obj (git_tag_free/git_tag_dup are git_object_free/git_object_dup). Every field is written by tag_parse before git_object_lookup publishes the object and never written afterwards, so shared handles read immutable state; the object keeps its repository uncounted (object.repo). Wrapped as Tag<'r> / TagArc<'r> in object/tag.rs (batch object wave-1 batch-3).

ptr.note: Allocated by tag_parse (the text after the blank line, NUL-terminated) and freed by git_tag__free; NULL for a tag without a message body. Read-only after the parse (git_tag_message lends it for the tag's lifetime).

Allocated (git__malloc, NUL-terminated copy of the 'tag ' header line) by tag_parse and freed by git_tag__free with the tag; NULL only while the zeroed object is being parsed or after a parse that failed before it. Read-only once the cache publishes the tag (git_tag_name lends it for the tag's lifetime).

One git_signature allocated by tag_parse when a 'tagger ' line is present, parsed in place by git_signature__parse, and freed (with its name and email) by git_signature_free in git_tag__free; NULL for a tag without a tagger. On a failed signature parse it stays set and git_object's error path frees it. Read-only after the parse (git_tag_tagger lends it). git_tag_create_from_buffer parses into a stack git_tag and frees these three fields itself.

types.name: git_time
types._comment_agent: Plain resource-free value (int64 seconds, int offset in minutes, char sign); no pointer field, no lifecycle routine: held by value (embedded in git_signature.when, copied field-wise by git_signature_dup/__pdup) and never released. git_signature_new sets sign = offset < 0 ? '-' : '+'. git_signature__parse leaves a calloc'd 0 sign/offset without a timezone, stores tz_start[0] verbatim as sign (any byte, not only '+'/'-') with offset 0 for a malformed timezone, and keeps the zeroes when hours > 14 or mins > 59. git_signature__writebuf (the one writer: commit, tag and reflog creation) prints '-' when offset < 0 or sign == '-' (the '-0000' case), '+' otherwise, hours/minutes from |offset| with %02d%02d, and the SECONDS THROUGH `(unsigned)sig->when.time` (%u): a time before the epoch or past 2106 is written wrapped modulo 2^32; it negates a negative offset as an int, so offset == INT_MIN overflows (C UB; the UBSan build aborts) - wrappers of the writing routines must refuse or document such a Time (core review wave 0, 2026-10-09; tests/equiv/types.rs::signature_zones_are_written_from_offset_and_sign). git_signature__equal compares the three fields. All-zero is a valid value. Wrapped as Time/TimeRef/TimeMut in core/types.rs (CZeroable, Copy, Send/Sync).

types.name: git_trace_level_t
types._comment_agent: C enum, values 0..6 (NONE..TRACE), passed by value. Consumers: git_trace_set stores any value in git_trace__data.level (GIT_ASSERT_ARG level == 0 || callback != NULL, an abort in Debug builds); git_trace() emits when git_trace__data.level >= level, so the integer order is the verbosity order; internal emitters only pass named levels (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE) to git_trace_cb. Wrapped as the fieldless TraceLevel enum (repr u32, Ord over the C values) with a fallible from_raw in core/trace.rs.

types.name: git_transaction
types._comment_agent: Opaque public type, no public fields. C discriminator owns two allocation shapes: pool containing tx (refs), standalone calloc (config). All pointer fields scalar. No clone. Free aborts pending work and owns teardown. Ref parent and config parent borrows must be retained. Internal config_new only used by public config_lock; backend reference acquisition occurs in its caller.

ptr.note: Config variant borrows config without up-ref; config owner must remain live through commit/free. Cleared after commit; NULL on refs variant.
Actually backend_instance*: git_config_lock increments its refcount after config_new; commit/free consumes via git_config_unlock, decrements and may free backend. NULL for refs or committed config.
Refs constructor obtains a counted git_repository_refdb reference, released by git_refdb_free after pending locks unlock; NULL for config.
Reference variant borrows repo, stores without up-ref; copy_common and refdb backend operations access it. NULL on config variant.

types.name: git_tree
types._comment_agent: git_tree is a git_object of type tree (first member `object`; casts both ways in object_api.c). It is opaque in the public API and refcounted through the embedded git_cached_obj (git_tree_free/git_tree_dup are git_object_free/git_object_dup). Its entries and odb_obj are filled by the parse before the cache publishes the tree and never written afterwards (tree iterators and treebuilder seeding only read them). It keeps its repository uncounted (object.repo), which git_tree_entry_bypath/git_tree_walk follow to load subtrees. Wrapped as Tree<'r> / TreeArc<'r> in object/tree.rs (batch object wave-1 batch-3).

ptr.note: git_array_t(git_tree_entry) owned by the tree: grown by git_array_alloc in git_tree__parse_raw (DEFAULT_TREE_SIZE initially) and freed by git_array_clear in git_tree__free; size entries are initialised. Each entry is by value and its filename borrows odb_obj's data (or the raw parse buffer). Read-only after the parse: git_tree_entry_byindex/_byname/_byid lend entries for the tree's lifetime.

One counted reference to the raw odb object (git_odb_object_dup in git_tree__parse), released by git_odb_object_free in git_tree__free; the entries' filenames point into its data. NULL for a tree parsed from a caller's buffer (git_tree__parse_raw via git_object__from_raw, git_object_rawcontent_is_valid), whose filenames then borrow that buffer for the call.

types.name: git_tree_entry
types._comment_agent: Two ownership forms. Owned: one git__calloc block (struct + name + NUL), from git_tree_entry_dup or git_tree_entry_bypath, released by git_tree_entry_free (git__free) and deep-copied by git_tree_entry_dup; it holds no reference to a tree or repository, so it may outlive both. Borrowed: an element of a git_tree's entries array (git_tree_entry_byindex/byname/byid) or a treebuilder's map (git_treebuilder_get), tied to its parent; git_treebuilder_insert rewrites attr and oid of an existing builder entry in place. No routine writes an entry through const git_tree_entry*. Rust: CBox<TreeEntry, TreeEntryFree> + TreeEntryRef<'a>.

ptr.note: NUL-terminated, filename_len bytes long. In an entry from alloc_entry (git_tree_entry_dup, git_tree_entry_bypath, the treebuilder) it points inline, right past the struct in the same git__calloc block; in an entry of a parsed tree's entries array it points into the tree's odb_obj data, which the tree keeps until git_tree__free frees the array with it. Either way it lives exactly as long as the entry's own storage and is never freed separately.

types.name: git_tree_update
types._comment_agent: git_tree_update is a plain caller-built value: libgit2 never allocates, copies or frees one and has no init/new/free routine for it (no lifecycle primitives). git_tree_create_updated reads a caller array of nupdates of them through a const pointer, sorting pointers to the elements (git_vector of &updates[i]) without copying or writing them. action is read in a switch (unnamed values -> GIT_ERROR_TREE 'unknown action for update'); id is copied into a tree builder entry (upsert only); filemode is checked against the existing entry's type and by git_treebuilder_insert (upsert only); for a removal only path is read. Wrapped as a Rust-owned, Copy, layout-transparent TreeUpdate<'p> whose slice is the C array.

ptr.note: Caller-owned NUL-terminated path ('/'-separated, from the root tree). Only git_tree_create_updated and its qsort comparator compare_entries read it (strcmp, git_fs_path_common_dirlen, count_slashes, strchr in next_component, git_fs_path_basename, error formatting), for the duration of that call; nothing stores, writes, duplicates or frees it. NULL is never checked: strcmp/strchr/basename dereference it, so it must be non-NULL. In Rust it is a &'p CStr carried by TreeUpdate<'p>.

types.name: git_treebuilder
types._comment_agent: Opaque in the public API (forward-declared in git2/types.h): no field is published. Heap-only, allocated by git_treebuilder_new (git__calloc), released by git_treebuilder_free; git_treebuilder_clear frees the entries but keeps the builder usable. No copy routine, no refcount, no lock. map owns its git_tree_entry values (alloc_entry, freed by clear/remove/filter); write_cache is a git_str scratch buffer disposed by free. Rust: TreeBuilder<'r> in object/tree.rs, owned by TreeBuilderBox<'r> = CBox<TreeBuilder<'r>, TreeBuilderFree>; neither Send nor Sync, since it reaches the repository (not Sync) through repo.

ptr.note: Set once by git_treebuilder_new from its non-NULL (GIT_ASSERT_ARG) repo argument and never reassigned; git_treebuilder_free never releases it (git_repository keeps no count). Followed by check_entry (git_treebuilder_insert / append_entry with validate) through git_object__is_valid, and by git_treebuilder__write_with_buffer (bld->repo->oid_type, git_repository_odb__weakptr, git_odb_write), which may lazily load and store the repository's odb: written through, so mutable. The repository must outlive the builder: Rust carries it as the builder's 'r borrow of a RepositoryRef.

types.name: git_treewalk_mode
types._comment_agent: C enum passed by value, values 0 (GIT_TREEWALK_PRE) and 1 (GIT_TREEWALK_POST); no pointer fields, no lifecycle. Sole consumer git_tree_walk refuses any other value with GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'invalid walking mode for tree walk' and -1 before touching the tree or calling back. PRE calls back for an entry before descending into its subtree and a positive callback result skips that subtree; POST calls back after the subtree and ignores positive results; a negative result stops both and is returned (GIT_ERROR_CALLBACK set if no error exists). Internal callers pass only named values (index.c read_tree POST, pack-objects.c PRE). Wrapped as the fieldless WalkMode enum (repr u32, PreOrder/PostOrder) with a fallible from_raw / TryFrom (UnnamedWalkMode) in object/tree.rs.

types.name: git_worktree
types._comment_agent: git_worktree is opaque in the public API (forward-declared in git2/types.h); its body is private to src/libgit2/worktree.h and only worktree.c, repository.c (git_repository_open_from_worktree) and submodule.c (get_url_base) read fields. Sole owner, no refcount, no lock, no copy routine: CBox<Worktree, WorktreeFree> with git_worktree_free (frees six strings then the struct, NULL is a no-op). Constructors, all alloc through an out-param and all needing a git_repository: git_worktree_lookup (sets *out NULL first), git_worktree_open_from_repository (does NOT reset *out on failure and has no GIT_ASSERT_ARG on repo), git_worktree_add (needs git_worktree_add_options). Every string is copied (strdup / read from the worktree's files / prettified), so a worktree never borrows the repository it was looked up in and may outlive it. Only git_worktree_lock / git_worktree_unlock write through the struct (the `locked` bit, which nothing reads back); every other consumer reads.

ptr.note: Parent repository's common dir, read from `<gitdir>/commondir` by git_worktree__read_link. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Prettified path of `<commondir>/worktrees/<name>/`, detached from a git_str. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Path of the working tree's `.git` file, read from `<gitdir>/gitdir` by git_worktree__read_link (made absolute against the gitdir when relative). Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Worktree name: git__strdup of the lookup name, or git_fs_path_basename of the worktree repo's gitdir in open_from_repository; returned borrowed by git_worktree_name. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Parent working directory: git__strdup of git_repository_workdir(repo) in git_worktree_lookup (NULL when the repository is bare) or of the prettified `<commondir>/..` in open_from_repository. git_worktree_validate and get_url_base check it for NULL. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

Working directory: git_fs_path_dirname(gitlink_path); returned borrowed by git_worktree_path. Allocated from libgit2's allocator by open_worktree_dir (behind git_worktree_lookup, git_worktree_open_from_repository and git_worktree_add) and released by git_worktree_free with git__free; never written through or replaced after construction.

types.name: git_worktree_add_options
types._comment_agent: Caller-built by-value options (stack in C), filled by git_worktree_add_options_init / GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_INIT, never allocated or freed by libgit2; git_worktree_add (the only consumer) refuses version 0 or >1 via GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION, memcpys it, reads lock and checkout_existing as C booleans (nonzero), dups ref, and copies checkout_options by value into git_checkout_head. No release, dispose or clone primitive; the embedded git_checkout_options borrows its own strings/paths/index/payloads. Review (wave 1 type review): a failing checkout through the embedded checkout_options (e.g. target_directory naming an existing file: git_checkout_head fails GIT_EEXISTS 'failed to make directory ...: directory exists') happens AFTER git_worktree_add has written worktrees/<name>/{commondir,gitdir,HEAD,refs/} and <wt>/.git and run git_refdb_init, so it leaves a lookup-able, never checked-out worktree whose HEAD holds the branch checked out; *out stays NULL and a retry of the same name fails 'reference ... is already checked out' (-1). The same for any later failure (git_repository_open, git_worktree_lookup); a failed git_futils_mkdir(worktree) (path exists / parent missing) leaves only the admin dir, which makes a retry GIT_EEXISTS.

ptr.note: The caller's attached reference, borrowed for the git_worktree_add call: git_worktree_add memcpys the options, tests git_reference_is_branch (name only), then git_reference_dup's it (reads name/target/peel, bumps the refdb count, never writes the reference) and frees only its own copy. NULL means 'branch named after the worktree' (checkout_existing) or a new branch at HEAD. Must be attached: dup copies ->db, and git_branch_is_checked_out reaches db->repo, so an unattached reference (NULL db) crashes and a reference outliving its repository reads a freed repo. git_worktree_add_options_init writes NULL; nothing frees it.

types.name: git_worktree_prune_options
types._comment_agent: Resource-free POD of two 32-bit scalars (8 bytes, no padding, no pointer). No dropper, disposer or cloner: callers hold it by value (stack) and C copies it by value. Its one lifecycle primitive is the in-place init constructor git_worktree_prune_options_init(opts, version), which memcpys GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_INIT = {1, 0} and fails (git_error_set GIT_ERROR_INVALID, opts untouched) only for version 0 or > GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_VERSION. All-zero is NOT the default: consumers (git_worktree_is_prunable, git_worktree_prune) reject version 0 with -1 'invalid version 0 on git_worktree_prune_options'. Consumers take it nullable and read-only (version check, then memcpy into a local); flags bits outside git_worktree_prune_t are ignored. Not shared with threads by C; no lock.

types.name: git_worktree_prune_t
types._comment_agent: Flag enum: VALID=1<<0, LOCKED=1<<1, WORKING_TREE=1<<2, OR-ed into git_worktree_prune_options.flags (uint32_t). C tests each bit with & and ignores the others, so any u32 is a valid flags value; the enum names single bits only.

types.name: git_writestream
types._comment_agent: git_writestream is a vtable header embedded as the first member of a concrete stream (blob_writestream, buffered_stream, buf_stream, checkout_stream, user filter streams); its three members take the header pointer and cast it back to the container, so a header is never valid detached from its container (never copied or held by value). Ownership: git_blob_create_from_stream returns an owned stream (released by its own `free`, or consumed by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit); git_filter_list_stream_{buffer,file,blob} borrow a caller target for the call and write/close (never free) it; a user filter's git_filter_stream_fn returns an owned stream to libgit2, which frees it with its `free` member after closing the chain, and gets `next` borrowed for the chain's life. Rust wrapper: WriteStream/WriteStreamRef/WriteStreamMut (core/types.rs), WriteStreamBox = CBox<WriteStream, WriteStreamFree> (free through the object's own member), RustWriteStream<W: StreamWriter> for Rust implementations.

ptr.note: Function pointer, set once at construction, never NULL. Finishes the stream; afterwards only `free` is valid (buf_stream/checkout_stream GIT_ASSERT on a second close, buffered_stream reruns its filter and closes its target again, blob close zeroes the filebuf so commit/write call a NULL fn). git_filter_list_stream_* call it exactly once on the head of the chain, and each buffered stream closes its target once; the user-supplied target is closed but never freed by libgit2. git_blob_create_from_stream documents that its stream must not be closed by the caller (commit flushes the filebuf close discarded).

Function pointer, set once at construction, never NULL: the stream's own destructor, releasing the CONTAINING object (blob_writestream_free: filebuf cleanup + git__free(hintpath) + git__free(stream); buffered_stream_free: disposes its bufs + git__free; buf_stream_free / checkout_stream_free: no-op for stack streams). It is the type's dropper, recoverable from the object, so the Rust release strategy (WriteStreamFree) is stateless. Valid after close or without close. libgit2 frees the streams it creates (filter_streams_free) and a user filter's stream returned through git_filter_stream_fn, never the caller's target; git_blob_create_from_stream_commit frees its argument.

Function pointer (code, static lifetime), set once by every producer at construction (blob_writestream_write, buffered_stream_write, buf_stream_write, checkout_stream_write) and never rewritten; never NULL. Called as stream->write(stream, buf, len) with `stream` = the header itself, which each implementation casts back to its container struct (git_writestream is the first member `parent`/`base`), so the member is only valid for the object it was read from. `< 0` is failure (callers test `< 0`; buffered_stream_close tests `== 0`). Calling it after `close` is invalid: blob streams then call a NULL filebuf write fn (git_filebuf_cleanup zeroes the filebuf), checkout streams write to a closed (possibly reused) fd, buf_stream fails GIT_ASSERT (abort in Debug builds).

The blob_writestream header (cast back to its container), released with its filebuf and hintpath; installed as git_writestream.free by git_blob_create_from_stream, and called by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit and on its own error path.

The buffered_stream header (cast back to its container); disposes input/temp_buf and git__frees the container, leaving the target alone. Installed as git_writestream.free; called by filter_streams_free.
libc calloc: ZEROING; NULL on overflow or failure. Released by free.
libc free: releases malloc/calloc/realloc storage; NULL is a no-op.
git__malloc(nelem*elsize) then memset 0: ZEROING; NULL on multiplication overflow (no error set) or OOM. Internal; released by git__free.

git__allocator.gfree(ptr): releases any git__malloc-family storage without reading it; NULL is a no-op (stdalloc free, failalloc no-op). Internal; publicly reachable only through git_odb_backend_data_free.

git__allocator.gmalloc(len): NON-zeroing; NULL on OOM with git_error_set_oom; always NULL before git_libgit2_init (failalloc). Internal (hidden visibility); publicly reachable only through git_odb_backend_data_alloc. Released by git__free.
git__reallocarray(NULL, nelem, elsize): NON-zeroing array storage; NULL on overflow or OOM. Internal; released by git__free.
Read for strlen(str)+1 bytes during the call only; NULL is dereferenced (crash), so not nullable.

Fresh git__malloc(strlen(str)+1) storage holding a copy of str with its terminator: the NUL-terminated string cloner behind git_strarray_copy, git_signature_new/dup and most libgit2 string fields. NULL on OOM (git_error_set_oom via git__malloc; before git_libgit2_init every request fails). Internal (hidden visibility): Rust reproduces it as OdbDataStrFree::dup / str_dup over git_odb_backend_data_alloc; released by git__free, publicly git_odb_backend_data_free.
Read for p_strnlen(str, n) bytes during the call only: a NUL within the first n bytes ends the copy, so the input may be an unterminated run of n bytes.

Fresh git__malloc(len+1) storage holding the first len = strnlen(str, n) bytes of str plus a terminator: a bounded string cloner. NULL on OOM. Internal; released by git__free (publicly git_odb_backend_data_free).
Read for exactly n bytes during the call only, NUL or not: the caller bounds the run (a path component, a token).

Fresh git__malloc(n+1) storage holding the n bytes at str plus a terminator: a byte-run-to-string cloner. NULL on OOM or when n+1 overflows to 0 only through malloc(0) semantics (no overflow check). Internal; released by git__free (publicly git_odb_backend_data_free).
Consumes the object: NULL is a no-op; REAL frees commit/tree/strings, VIRTUAL frees index/parents, any other type aborts; then git__free of the struct. Never touches the repository.
NUL-terminated string read for the call and copied (git__strdup), never retained
object id, read for the call (git_commit_lookup); any type byte reaches C

Out slot: receives a fresh REAL annotated commit (git__calloc'd) owned by the caller, released by git_annotated_commit_free. Written by the lookup on success; then two git__strdup calls (branch_name, remote_url) — if either fails it returns -1 with *out STILL SET, so the caller must free it. A failed lookup returns -1, not its code.
NUL-terminated string read for the call and copied (git__strdup), never retained
repository, borrowed for the call: commit lookup through its odb and object cache; not retained by the annotated commit itself (its commit object keeps an unowned back-pointer).

Out slot: receives a fresh REAL annotated commit (git__calloc'd) owned by the caller, released by git_annotated_commit_free. Set to NULL first; on success then git__strdup(ref name) — if that fails it returns -1 with *out STILL SET (ref_name NULL), so the caller must free it.
reference, read for the call (git_reference_peel, git_reference_name); its name is copied
repository, borrowed for the call: commit lookup through its odb and object cache; not retained by the annotated commit itself (its commit object keeps an unowned back-pointer).

Out slot: receives a fresh REAL annotated commit (git__calloc'd) owned by the caller, released by git_annotated_commit_free. Not cleared before git_revparse_single/git_object_peel: on their failure *out is untouched; annotated_commit_init sets it NULL then writes on success.
repository, borrowed for the call: commit lookup through its odb and object cache; not retained by the annotated commit itself (its commit object keeps an unowned back-pointer).
NUL-terminated string read for the call and copied (git__strdup), never retained
object id, read for the call (git_commit_lookup); any type byte reaches C
Out slot: receives a fresh REAL annotated commit (git__calloc'd) owned by the caller, released by git_annotated_commit_free. Set to NULL first; written only on success.
repository, borrowed for the call: commit lookup through its odb and object cache; not retained by the annotated commit itself (its commit object keeps an unowned back-pointer).
`len` bytes, read during the call only by git_odb_stream_write; any content (NUL bytes included). Must be valid for `len` bytes even when len is 0 (passed to memcpy).
Out-parameter (GIT_ASSERT_ARG / written unconditionally on success): the new object's id, written only on success.
Live repository for the call; libgit2 loads and caches its odb (atomic CAS on repo->_odb) and other caches through it, so it is written though shared. Not retained.
Out-parameter (GIT_ASSERT_ARG / written unconditionally on success): the new object's id, written only on success.

Filesystem path (absolute or relative to the process cwd), prettified with realpath; read for the call only. When it falls under the working directory, the remainder is the relative hint path that loads filters.
Live repository for the call; libgit2 loads and caches its odb (atomic CAS on repo->_odb) and other caches through it, so it is written though shared. Not retained.
Optional filter hint path; git__strdup'd into the stream, so borrowed for the call only.

Out-slot (GIT_ASSERT_ARG): on success receives a fresh git__calloc'd blob_writestream header, owned by the caller and released by its own `free` member or consumed by git_blob_create_from_stream_commit; untouched on failure.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; stored unretained in the stream (stream->repo), which commit later uses: the repository must outlive the stream.

Must be a stream from git_blob_create_from_stream (cast to blob_writestream unchecked) that was never closed (close zeroes the filebuf; the flush then calls a NULL write fn). Consumed on every path: blob_writestream_free runs on success and failure.
Out-parameter: the new blob's id, written on success only (git_blob__create_from_paths).
Out-parameter (GIT_ASSERT_ARG / written unconditionally on success): the new object's id, written only on success.

Path relative to the working directory, joined onto it and used as the filter hint path; read for the call only. An absolute path reaches the attr lookup's GIT_ASSERT(!absolute), which aborts a _DEBUG build.

Live repository for the call; libgit2 loads and caches its odb (atomic CAS on repo->_odb) and other caches through it, so it is written though shared. Not retained. Fails with -1 (GIT_ERROR_REPOSITORY, no working directory) when bare/pathless.

Read-only byte buffer of `len` bytes, not NUL-terminated (may contain NUL, which is itself the binary signal). Read only during the call via git_str_attach_notowned (not owned, never freed or retained). A refcount down-ref (GIT_REFCOUNT_DEC): NULL is a no-op; the atomic count drops by one, and odb_free runs only when it reaches 0 while no repository owns the odb (rc.owner NULL): every backend's own free, the commit-graph, the backend vector, own_cache, the mutex, then git__free. Overwritten without releasing what it held (count = 0, commits = NULL first), so a wrapper must clear a reused CommitArray first (CommitArrayMut::clear). On success: the HEAD commit then each MERGE_HEAD commit, as git_commit_lookup references in a git_vector_detach'd libgit2 buffer the caller owns (git_commitarray_dispose). {NULL, 0} for an unborn HEAD (returns 0) and on failure. C DEFECT: on a failure after the first parent is collected (malformed MERGE_HEAD line: 'unable to parse OID - invalid length'; or a MERGE_HEAD id that is not a commit, which insert_mergehead turns into -1), done: frees the collected commits with git__free instead of git_commit_free while the repository's object cache still holds them: the next lookup of that commit, or the cache teardown in git_repository_free, is a heap-use-after-free (ASan-confirmed, repository wave 0 batch 2). The safe wrapper must not reach it (e.g. pre-validate MERGE_HEAD, or rebuild the routine over revparse + mergehead_foreach in Rust). Further C defects (repository wave 1 batch 2): HEAD resolving to a non-commit is put in the array as a commit (a tag object, or a blob/tree, read later through git_commit_* as the wrong struct); and git_revparse_ext leaks HEAD's reference when HEAD names a missing or unreadable object (revparse_lookup_object drops `ref` when git_object_lookup fails; LSan). The Rust RepositoryRef::commit_parents is a composition (Replaces anchor): git_reference_dwim("HEAD") + git_object_lookup(ANY) (freeing the reference on every path), git_object_peel to COMMIT (tags peel, others GIT_EINVALIDSPEC), git_repository_mergehead_foreach + git_commit_lookup into a Rust Vec released by git_commit_free on error, and an OdbDataVec buffer adopted by CommitArray::from_raw.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Read (revparse HEAD, MERGE_HEAD) and its object cache updated by the lookups; not retained by the result: the commits outlive the repository.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(NULL); only read.
repo->commondir, set at open and freed only by git_repository_free; NULL for git_repository_new (in-memory). Borrowed for the repository's life (RepositoryRef<'a> -> Option<&'a CStr>).

Receives an up-ref'd (GIT_REFCOUNT_INC) reference to the repository's lazily loaded config (repo->_config, owner = repo), released by git_config_free: a SHARED reference (ConfigArc), since the repository holds and writes through another. On a load failure __weakptr still writes *out = repo->_config, i.e. NULL, and -1 is returned before the up-ref. The reference BORROWS the repository (ConfigArc<'r> of the RepositoryRef<'r>): git_repository_free disowns the config (rc.owner = NULL) before its down-ref, so the config may be released after the repository, but every file backend load_config added keeps `repo` (config_file_open: b->repo, uncounted and never cleared) and reparses its file through it for includeIf conditions (config_file_refresh on a changed file from config_file_get / config_file_iterator; config_file_refresh_from_buffer after config_file_write): `gitdir:` reads git_repository__item_path(repo), `onbranch:` runs git_repository_refdb(repo), a write. ASan-confirmed heap-use-after-free (review wave 1 batch 1) through set_config into another repository + set_bare after the lender was freed.
Not asserted (dereferenced unconditionally). Its config slot is set with a compare-and-swap on first load.

Out slot: NULLed by git_config_snapshot, then a fresh git_config_new config (count 1, no owner) holding snapshots of the repo config's backends: the caller's sole reference (ConfigBox), released by git_config_free. Untouched if the repo config itself fails to load (returns that error first).
Loads and caches repo->_config (weak) through the shared pointer; not retained by the snapshot.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call. A missing or unresolvable start ("" included) fails ENOTFOUND.

Opaque payload passed through to cb, never dereferenced or kept past the call.

Released: cleanup drops the counted odb/refdb/config/index references, then every owned string, cache and array, then the struct (git__free). NULL is a no-op.

Reads repo->gitdir; GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(repo, NULL).
repo->gitdir, owned by the repository and freed with it; assigned only by the open routines, never replaced afterwards. NULL for a repository without a git directory (git_repository_new, wrap_odb).

Out slot: one new counted reference to the repository's refdb (lazily opened, rc.owner = repo); released with git_refdb_free. The refdb and its backend keep an uncounted pointer to the repository (db->repo), so the reference must not outlive it. Untouched on failure (-1).
Lazily opens and installs repo->_refdb (cache fill).

Rewrites the repository's config file (core.* fs probes) at <gitdir>/config, clears the configmap cache, and with recurse reinitialises submodules (errors ignored). A pathless repository writes ./config in the cwd (probed).
Writes core.bare/core.worktree through the repo config, frees repo->workdir and sets is_bare; a no-op returning 0 when already bare.

Retained: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo; the caller keeps its own reference. GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL. A sole caller reference stops being sole. The repository keeps the reference until freed or given another config and reparses the config's files through it (any git_config_set_* via __weakptr: set_bare, set_workdir), which evaluates includeIf conditions against the repository each file backend was loaded for (config_file_backend.repo, uncounted): only a config loaded for no repository (ConfigArc<'static>: git_config_new + files added with repo NULL, a snapshot) may be installed; one git_repository_config lent borrows its repository, which this one may outlive (review wave 1 batch 1, ASan use-after-free).
Swaps repo->_config: the old one is disowned (OWN NULL) and released.
Reference name read for the call (GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL); copied into the new HEAD.
Reads/writes HEAD and the reflog through the repository's refdb (lazily opened); the struct itself only gets cache fills.
Id read for the call (GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL). Looked up with git_object_lookup: an id of another type than the repository's overflows the loose path buffer (SHA256 id in SHA1 repo).
As set_head; also looks the id up through the object db (cache fill).
Read for the call: its id and description (the reflog's target name). GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL. Same id-type hazard as set_head_detached when the commit comes from a repository of another type.
As set_head_detached.
Copied with git__strdup; NULL clears.
Copied with git__strdup; NULL clears. On an email strdup failure the name copy leaks.

Retained when non-NULL: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo (caller keeps its reference). NULL removes the repository's index.

Copied with git__strdup; NULL clears the namespace.
Frees repo->namespace (which git_repository_get_namespace lent) and stores a copy; no NULL check on repo. On strdup failure namespace is left NULL and -1 returned.
Retained: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo, overwriting any previous owner silently (the first owner's lookups then use the new owner's cache). GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.
Swaps repo->_odb: the old one is disowned and released.

Retained: GIT_REFCOUNT_INC + rc.owner = repo. db->repo (the repository it was opened for) is NOT updated: the installing repository then dereferences that repository on every ref operation, so it must outlive them. GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.
Swaps repo->_refdb: the old one is disowned and released.

Path read for the call (prettified copy stored); GIT_ASSERT_ARG non-NULL.

HAZARD: with a NULL gitdir (git_repository_new / wrap_odb) git_str_joinpath treats NULL as "" and the files backend uses NULL paths too, so it removes those names relative to the process's cwd; the safe wrapper refuses such a repository (ENOTFOUND, 'path cannot exist in repository'). Wrapped on RepositoryMut.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. git_submodule_cache_free(repo->submodule_cache) (NULL no-op; drops each cached submodule's reference, then the map and struct) and NULLs the slot; always returns 0. Also run by git_repository__cleanup / free. Submodules looked up through the cache hold their own reference and survive.

repo->workdir (with trailing slash), or NULL for a bare repository or one without paths. Out slot: written only on success with a git_signature_now result owned by the caller.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call and copied (trimmed) into fresh libgit2-allocated strings, never retained.

As git_tag_list: caller-owned array of libgit2-allocated strings, git_strarray_dispose; on internal failure NULL/0 with return 0 and leaked names.
Read for the call, never retained; its oid type is not checked against the repository's (an id of another type overflows or underfills the loose backend's path, see git_object_lookup).

On success one counted reference to the repository's cached parsed tag (shared with the cache and every other lookup of the id, as git_tag or git_object), or a freshly parsed one; git_object_lookup* behind a cast with type GIT_OBJECT_TAG, so an object of another type is GIT_ENOTFOUND. It keeps repo uncounted in object.repo, so it must not be used past repo. Untouched on failure.
Its odb is loaded lazily and its object cache filled; the result keeps this pointer uncounted.

Read for the call, never retained; its oid type is not checked against the repository's (an id of another type overflows or underfills the loose backend's path, see git_object_lookup). At most (len + 1) / 2 bytes are copied, with the id's type byte, into the search key.

On success one counted reference to the repository's cached parsed tag (shared with the cache and every other lookup of the id, as git_tag or git_object), or a freshly parsed one; git_object_lookup* behind a cast with type GIT_OBJECT_TAG, so an object of another type is GIT_ENOTFOUND. It keeps repo uncounted in object.repo, so it must not be used past repo. Untouched on failure. The prefix must name exactly one object of the database, whatever its type, which must then be a tag.
Its odb is loaded lazily and its object cache filled; the result keeps this pointer uncounted.
Live tag, only read; NULL refused by assert (returns NULL).
t->message: NULL when the content ends with the header; otherwise a NUL-terminated copy owned by the tag (embedded NULs truncate the C view).
Live tag, only read; NULL is refused by GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL (returns NULL).
t->tag_name: NUL-terminated copy the parse allocates (non-NULL on parse success), freed by git_tag__free with the tag.

NUL-terminated tag name, read during the call only and copied into a temporary git_str (git__malloc; needs initialized runtime, else allocation fails with -1). NULL yields *valid = 0 and returns 0. An invalid name leaves a GIT_ERROR_REFERENCE error set (from git_reference__normalize_name) while returning 0; only OOM returns < 0.
Out-parameter: written 0 first, then 1 if `refs/tags/<name>` is a valid reference name. NULL fails GIT_ASSERT (returns -1, sets GIT_ERROR_INTERNAL).
Live tag, only read (git_object_owner behind a cast).
obj->repo: the repository the tag was looked up in, stored without a count and never cleared; borrowed from whoever owns the repository (the tag must not outlive it). Non-NULL for any looked-up tag.
Live tag, read; its repository is used for each lookup.
Out slot: on success one counted reference to the first non-tag object of the chain (git_object_peel with GIT_OBJECT_ANY), released with git_object_free. Untouched on failure.
Live tag, only read; no NULL check (NULL crashes).
t->tagger: NULL for a taggerless tag; else a git_signature the tag owns (git_tag__free frees it). Its name/email may be NULL if git_signature__parse ran out of memory copying them.
Live tag, only read; its repository (uncounted) is used for the lookup, so it must be live and its cache is filled.

Out slot: on success one counted reference to the target object (git_object_lookup of t->target with t->type through t->object.repo), released with git_object_free; it keeps the repository uncounted. Untouched on failure.
Live tag, only read; NULL refused by assert (returns NULL).
&t->target: the parsed target id, of the repository's oid type; valid as long as the tag.
Live tag, only read; NULL refused by assert (returns GIT_OBJECT_INVALID). Parse guarantees one of commit/tree/blob/tag.

Sole invoker git_trace__write_fmt (src/libgit2/trace.h, via git_trace) passes git_str_cstr of a local git_str it formats the message into and disposes right after the call: borrowed for the call only, never NULL (an allocated string, or the static git_str__initstr / git_str__oom sentinel after a failed vprintf), NUL-terminated, arbitrary bytes (server responses are traced verbatim, so not necessarily UTF-8). git_trace call sites: transports/httpclient.c (DEBUG 'Connecting to remote/proxy', 'Sending ... request'; TRACE 'Received:' and the request dump) in every build, and streams/stransport.c:269 (INFO, an SSLRead error) only under GIT_HTTPS_SECURETRANSPORT, out of the campaign's scope. The level argument is always a named GIT_TRACE_* constant at every call site (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE in practice; never NONE). Called on whichever thread runs the traced libgit2 call, concurrently from several threads; the callback reads no payload (none exists), and git_trace__data is read without a lock.

Function pointer stored verbatim in the unlocked global git_trace__data.callback and called (by git_trace, from any thread running the HTTP client) until the next git_trace_set: borrowed for as long as it stays installed, never released. NULL only with level == 0 (GIT_ASSERT_ARG: -1 GIT_ERROR_INVALID in release, abort in debug). git_trace reads level/callback without a lock and re-reads callback after the NULL check (TOCTOU), so a set racing a trace is a data race and clearing can make C call NULL.
Retained borrowed parent, must outlive transaction. No parent reference increment.
Scalar backend_instance erased to void; config_new stores it without up-ref. Its only caller config_lock locks backend then increments reference; commit/free consumes through config_unlock.
Writable caller slot; success transfers one fresh transaction, failure leaves unchanged.
Consumes initialized refs/config transaction, aborts remaining locks, releases counted dependencies and matching allocation; NULL no-op.
Writable caller slot; success transfers one fresh transaction, failure leaves unchanged.
Retained borrowed parent, must outlive transaction. No parent reference increment.

Optional tree; git_tree_dup'd and freed within the call, entries copied into the root builder. Its subtrees are looked up in repo by id, so its id type must match repo's (else the loose path is formatted out of bounds).
Written with the new root tree id on success.
Live repository; odb loaded and written, cache filled; every builder keeps it uncounted for the call only.

Array of nupdates git_tree_update read in place for the call (sorted by path into a vector of pointers, never copied or retained). Each path is dereferenced unchecked (non-NULL); upsert ids reach git_treebuilder_insert's object lookup (type must match repo's), components > 65535 bytes are truncated into a corrupt tree.
git_object_dup behind a cast; not NULL-checked: the atomic refcount is incremented in place, so obj must be live; the same pointer is handed back through out.
Receives obj itself, one more reference counted on it; always 0.

Not NULL-checked: git_oid_equal memcmps the whole git_oid (type byte and all 32 id bytes) against each entry's, for the call only. An id of another type, or a SHA-1 id with non-zero tail bytes, matches nothing; reads stay within the struct.
Asserted non-NULL; entries scanned linearly, only read.
First entry whose id equals id, or NULL (no error set). An element of tree->entries, valid while the tree lives. Rust: Option<TreeEntryRef<'a>>.
Asserted non-NULL; only read (git_array_get bounds-checks idx).
NULL when idx >= entrycount (no error set); else &tree->entries.ptr[idx], live and unchanged while the tree lives. Rust: Option<TreeEntryRef<'a>>.

NUL-terminated name, strlen'd and compared for the call only; asserted non-NULL. Longer than UINT16_MAX: TREE_ENTRY_CHECK_NAMELEN sets GIT_ERROR_INVALID 'tree entry path too long' yet goes on with the length truncated to 16 bits for the homing compare (reads stay within the name) and the full length for the match, so NULL.
Asserted non-NULL (else NULL, GIT_ERROR_INVALID). Only read: binary homing search over tree->entries then a linear scan.

NULL on a miss (no error set, except for an overlong name). Otherwise an element of tree->entries, whose filename points into the tree's odb_obj data: valid while the tree lives, never written after the parse, never freed by the caller. Rust: TreeEntryRef<'a> tied to the shared tree borrow.

On success a fresh entry from git_tree_entry_dup (one block: struct and inline name) the caller frees with git_tree_entry_free; it keeps nothing of the tree or its repository. Untouched on failure (every subtree looked up on the way is freed).
NUL-terminated, read for the call, split on '/': an empty component is 'invalid tree path given'; a trailing '/' is accepted after a tree entry only.

Read for the call: its entries by name; for a path of several components the subtrees are looked up through root->object.repo (uncounted), so the tree's repository must be live and used by this thread only. Must be a tree object: a commit/blob/tag pointer is read as a tree.
Read for the call: filename, filename_len, attr. Not asserted non-NULL.
As e1.
Receives a fresh alloc_entry block owned by the caller, freed by git_tree_entry_free; untouched on failure (-1, out of memory).
Read for the call (name, length, oid, attr); may be owned or borrowed from a tree/treebuilder.
Reads entry->attr and normalises it; not asserted non-NULL.
Reads entry->attr as stored; not asserted non-NULL.

git__free of the entry's single block (struct + inline name); only valid for entries from git_tree_entry_dup / git_tree_entry_bypath, never for ones borrowed from a tree or treebuilder. NULL is a no-op.
NULL returns NULL via GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL.
&entry->oid: lives inside the entry (owned block, tree's entries array, or builder entry); NULL only for a NULL entry.
NULL returns NULL via GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL.
entry->filename: NUL-terminated, inline after an owned entry, or pointing into the tree's odb data / builder entry; lives as long as the entry's owner.
Only its id is read; not retained.
git_object_lookup(entry->oid, ANY): one counted reference (cache or fresh parse) the caller releases with git_object_free.

Repository the object is looked up in (odb load, cache fill); not asserted non-NULL here (git_object_lookup asserts). The entry's id is formatted with the repo's oid length by the loose backend: an id of another type overflows/underfills.
Reads attr: gitlink -> COMMIT, dir -> TREE, else BLOB; NULL -> GIT_OBJECT_INVALID.
NULL asserts and returns 0; otherwise only tree->entries.size is read.
git_object_free behind a cast: gives up one counted reference (git_cached_obj_decref); at zero git_tree__free runs, which never reads object.repo. NULL is a no-op.
git_object_id behind a cast; asserted non-NULL; only read.
&obj->object.cached.oid: lives as long as the tree, written once at parse. Rust: OidRef<'a>.
Read for the call, never retained; its oid type is not checked against the repository's (an id of another type overflows or underfills the loose backend's path, see git_object_lookup).

Its odb is loaded lazily and its object cache filled; the result keeps this pointer uncounted.
git_object_owner behind a cast; asserted non-NULL; only read.

obj->object.repo, stored uncounted at lookup and never cleared: valid while the repository the tree was looked up in lives. Non-const: callers look objects up through it. Rust: RepositoryRef<'r>, the handle the tree was looked up through.

Not NULL-checked: called synchronously with (path, entry, payload) for each entry, path the subtree prefix ('' at the root, 'a/b/'), entry borrowed for the call (a subtree's entries are freed after it is walked). Negative stops, returned, with git_error_set_after_callback_function naming git_tree_walk only when no error is set; positive skips the subtree in pre-order, ignored in post-order.
Opaque payload passed through to callback, never dereferenced or kept past the call.

Not NULL-checked (dereferenced for its entries). Only read; each subtree is looked up through tree->object.repo (filling its cache) and freed once walked, so the repository must be live and usable on this thread.
Asserted non-NULL (the only failure, -1). Frees every owned entry and empties the map; the builder, its map storage and write_cache stay, so it remains usable. Returns 0.
Non-const in the signature but only reads the map size; NULL returns 0.
Asserted non-NULL. Iterates its entry map, removing and git_tree_entry_free'ing each entry the filter returns non-zero for; never reaches the repository. Always returns 0 otherwise.
Asserted non-NULL; called synchronously once per entry with (entry, payload); entry is freed right after a non-zero answer, so it is borrowed for the call only. Iteration cannot be stopped.
Opaque payload passed through to filter, never dereferenced or kept past the call.
The builder's own entry, lent for the call: git_treebuilder_filter removes and frees it right after a non-zero return.
Caller's payload passed through unchanged.
NULL is a no-op. Disposes write_cache, frees every entry (git_treebuilder_clear), disposes the map, then git__free's the builder. Never touches bld->repo.
Asserted non-NULL (else NULL with GIT_ERROR_INVALID). Only probes the entry map (read-only lookup, no error on a miss); declared non-const but never written.
NUL-terminated name, read for the call only (hashed/compared as the map key); asserted non-NULL.

NULL when the builder has no entry of that name (no error set). Otherwise the builder's own heap entry (struct + inline name), owned by its map: valid until the builder removes/replaces (insert updates oid/attr in place)/clears/filters it or is freed. Never freed by the caller. Rust: TreeEntryRef<'a> tied to the shared builder borrow.

Asserted non-NULL. Mutated: puts a new heap entry into its map, or overwrites an existing entry's oid and attr in place. Follows bld->repo (unowned) to check the object in the ODB, lazily loading the repository's odb.

Optional out-param (NULL = not wanted); the outer slot is written (mutable is false only because the innermost pointee is const),  only on success with the builder's own entry for filename (new or updated in place). The entry stays the builder's: valid until its next change (remove/replace/clear/filter/free). Rust: insert (out NULL) and insert_entry (TreeEntryRef tied to the exclusive borrow).

NUL-terminated name, asserted non-NULL; validated (non-empty, no traversal/.git/slash) and copied into the entry allocation; never retained. C defect: a name longer than UINT16_MAX bytes is accepted (TREE_ENTRY_CHECK_NAMELEN only sets GIT_ERROR_INVALID without failing), filename_len is truncated to uint16_t and git_treebuilder_write then stores a corrupt tree. Rust refuses > 65535 bytes before FFI.

Asserted non-NULL; zero id refused; copied by value (git_oid_cpy), not retained. Unless the mode is COMMIT (or invalid, refused first) or strict object creation is off, looked up in the ODB (git_object__is_valid -> git_odb_read_header) WITHOUT checking that its type is the repository's: the loose backend's object_file_name sizes the path for bld->repo's oid type but git_oid_pathfmt writes the id's own hex size, so a SHA-256 id in a SHA-1 repository writes 24 bytes past the git_str (ASan heap-buffer-overflow for objects paths under ~80 bytes), and a SHA-1 id in a SHA-256 repository leaves part of the path uninitialised. Callers must pass an id of the builder's repository type for looked-up modes; Rust refuses another type before FFI (id_fits against the builder's repo).

Out-parameter, asserted non-NULL. On success receives a fresh git__calloc'd builder the caller owns and releases with git_treebuilder_free; on failure (OOM, or append_entry failing for a source entry, which frees the half-built builder) it is left untouched.
Asserted non-NULL; stored unretained in bld->repo, so the repository must outlive the builder written to builder_p. Not read during construction (append_entry runs with validate=false).
Optional seed tree, only read during the call: each entry's filename and oid are copied into a new entry (alloc_entry), so the builder keeps nothing of it. NULL starts empty.

Asserted non-NULL via treebuilder_get. Removes the map slot and frees the removed entry (git_tree_entry_free), invalidating any pointer to it from get/insert. Does not reach the repository. -1 with GIT_ERROR_TREE when the name is absent.
NUL-terminated name read for the call (lookup key, and the error message); asserted non-NULL.

Asserted non-NULL. Writes its own write_cache buffer (cleared and refilled); entries only read (sorted into a temporary vector). Follows bld->repo (unowned) to lazily load the odb (git_repository_odb__weakptr) and git_odb_write; backend errors propagate with their codes.
Asserted non-NULL out id, written by git_odb_write on success (the repository's oid type).

root: tree_walk's git_str path ptr (GIT_STR_INIT => static empty string at the top), each subtree's name + '/'; never NULL (OOM is checked before recursing); lent for the call only, truncated/regrown afterwards.
entry: element of the walked (sub)tree's entries array; the subtree is git_tree_free'd after its walk, so valid for the call only. Never NULL.
Opaque caller payload passed through from git_tree_walk unchanged; libgit2 never dereferences it. Rust: points at the WalkCallback handle.
Worktree/branch name, joined unchecked to <commondir>/worktrees (".."/"/" escape); copied, not retained.

memcpy'd after the version check; ref is git_reference_dup'ed, checkout options copied and read for the inner git_checkout_head. NULL = defaults. git_branch_is_checked_out(ref) walks the worktrees of git_reference_owner(ref), the repository the reference was READ THROUGH, not of repo: a reference of another repository defeats the 'already checked out' refusal for repo's branch of that name (two of repo's worktrees on one branch) and triggers it for the other repository's checkout (review wave 2 batch 0, C-confirmed; the Rust wrapper looks the name up in repo and substitutes repo's own reference when found).

GIT_ASSERT_ARG, then set to NULL; receives the worktree git_worktree_lookup loads once the gitdir, working directory, refs and checkout are created, owned by the caller (git_worktree_free). Stays NULL on failure.

Read for commondir/HEAD; may create branch `name` through its refdb (reflog via git_signature_now). NULL commondir (pathless repo) makes it mkdir ./worktrees in the cwd, then prettify_dir(NULL) asserts and `(err = ... < 0)` returns 1 with *out NULL: wrapper refuses pathless repos.
Working directory path; only its last component is created (GIT_MKDIR_EXCL); copied, not retained.

Caller-provided storage, written in full by memcpy of GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_INIT ({1, 0, 0, NULL, GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT}) when version is in 1..=GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_VERSION; left untouched (error set, -1) otherwise. No NULL check: a NULL opts with a valid version is a NULL write. Reaches no allocator on success.

NULL is a no-op. Frees commondir_path, worktree_path, gitlink_path, gitdir_path, parent_path and name with git__free, then the struct. Releases every worktree the constructors hand out; also open_worktree_dir's error path, get_url_base, git_repository_foreach_worktree and git_repository_head_for_worktree on the worktrees they looked up.

Optional out buffer: NULL skips reading the reason. Otherwise converted with git_buf_tostr (takes over an owned buffer), cleared, filled with the `locked` file's contents when locked, and handed back with git_buf_fromstr (owned when allocated; static empty string when not locked). Caller disposes with git_buf_dispose. On a read error (e.g. `locked` is a directory) the buffer is left as converted.
Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Reads the file system (<gitdir>/locked), not wt->locked.

Read-only despite the non-const type: GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION reads version (NULL passes), then memcpy copies it into a local; NULL means the {VERSION, 0} defaults. Not retained past the call. Flag bits outside git_worktree_prune_t are ignored.

Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Not asserted. Returns 1 prunable, 0 not (the reason set as the thread's error), <0 on a version or locked-read error. Precedence slip `ret = (git_str_printf(..) < 0)` makes an OOM there return 1.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; reads repo->commondir only. HAZARD: NULL commondir (repository without paths) joins as "", listing <cwd>/worktrees/; the wrapper returns an empty list instead.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Overwritten with {NULL,0} first, without disposing what it held; on success receives a git_vector_detach'd array of git__strdup'd names owned by the caller (git_strarray_dispose); NULL/0 when worktrees/ is missing or empty. C DEFECT: entries failing is_worktree_dir are removed with git_vector_remove inside git_vector_foreach, so the entry after each removed one is never checked and is listed (C-confirmed: 4 junk dirs + 1 worktree lists a junk name). A dirload failure leaks the partial vector.
Optional lock reason, attached not-owned and written to the file; read for the call only. NULL = empty file.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Live worktree, WRITTEN: sets wt->locked = 1 after creating <gitdir>/locked (O_EXCL). Returns GIT_ELOCKED WITHOUT setting an error when already locked. Wrapped on WorktreeMut (the Worktree Sync proof relies on it).
GIT_ASSERT_ARG; joined into the worktree's gitdir path and git__strdup'd as its name, never retained.

Out slot, set to NULL after the asserts on repo and name (out itself is not asserted); receives a fresh git__calloc'd worktree whose strings are all copies, owned by the caller (git_worktree_free). Stays NULL on failure: GIT_ENOTFOUND when `<commondir>/worktrees/<name>` is not a directory, -1 when it lacks commondir/gitdir/HEAD or a link cannot be read.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG; read for the call (commondir, workdir), never retained: the worktree copies what it needs, so it may outlive the repository. HAZARD: repo->commondir goes to strlen through git_str_join3 unchecked, so a repository without paths (git_repository_new, wrap_odb: commondir NULL) is a NULL dereference; the wrapper refuses it first. Failures with no error message: GIT_ENOTFOUND (no such dir) and -1 (not a worktree dir).
GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(NULL); reads wt->name.
wt->name, a non-NULL git__strdup'd copy the worktree owns; freed only by git_worktree_free, so it borrows the worktree.

Out slot, NOT reset on failure (left as the caller initialised it); receives a fresh worktree owned by the caller (git_worktree_free) when repo is a worktree's repository. Fails with GIT_ERROR_WORKTREE 'cannot open worktree of a non-worktree repo' otherwise.
Not asserted: NULL dereferences in git_repository_is_worktree. Read for the call (gitdir, commondir), never retained.
GIT_ASSERT_ARG_WITH_RETVAL(NULL); reads wt->worktree_path.
wt->worktree_path, dirname of the gitdir link: a non-NULL copy the worktree owns, freed only by git_worktree_free, so it borrows the worktree.

Read-only despite the non-const type: GIT_ERROR_CHECK_VERSION reads version (NULL passes), then memcpy copies it into a local; NULL means the {VERSION, 0} defaults. Not retained past the call. Flag bits outside git_worktree_prune_t are ignored. HAZARD for the safe wrapper: prune tests `!git_worktree_is_prunable(wt, &popts)`, so an is_prunable ERROR (<0, e.g. GIT_ENOTFOUND 'requested file is a directory' when the `locked` entry cannot be read, checked only without GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_LOCKED) counts as prunable and prune deletes the gitdir anyway; git_futils_rmdir_r then clears the error state (pinned in tests/equiv/worktree.rs::prune_options::prune_reads_the_options_alike).

Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Not asserted. Deletes <commondir>/worktrees/<name> and, with PRUNE_WORKING_TREE, dirname(gitlink_path) on disk; the struct stays valid. Treats an is_prunable error as prunable (see opts); the safe wrapper calls is_prunable first and reports its error.

Caller-provided storage, written in full by memcpy of the {VERSION, 0} template when version is in 1..=GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_VERSION; left untouched (error set) otherwise. GIT_INIT_STRUCTURE_FROM_TEMPLATE has no NULL check: a NULL opts with a valid version is a NULL write.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Live worktree, WRITTEN: clears wt->locked after unlinking <gitdir>/locked. Returns 1 when not locked; a failed p_unlink (e.g. `locked` is a directory) returns -1 WITHOUT setting an error. Wrapped on WorktreeMut.

GIT_ASSERT_ARG. Live worktree, only read (its six owned strings); never retained. Checks gitdir_path (is_worktree_dir), parent_path (when set), commondir_path, worktree_path exist; GIT_ERROR + GIT_ERROR_WORKTREE message on the first missing.
Consumes entry and all three independently allocated optional strings using git__free. Internal static helper; public clients never release an entry directly.
libc malloc: NON-zeroing; NULL on failure. Called directly by the stdalloc/debugalloc backends of git__allocator and by vendored deps (ntlmclient, reftable's default). Released by free.
reftable_malloc(nelem*elsize) then memset 0: ZEROING; NULL on overflow, zero size or failure. Released by reftable_free.
reftable's free hook or libc free; NULL is a no-op. Releases reftable_malloc-family storage.

reftable's allocator: the hook set by reftable_set_alloc (libgit2 installs git__ wrappers in refdb_reftable.c) or malloc. NON-zeroing; returns NULL for sz == 0 and on failure. Released by reftable_free.
